docs.title: What is V-FOR-WaTer?
docs.text:
V-FOR-WaTer brings together environmental data, computational tools, and research workflows in a common digital environment. The goal is that researchers and other interested users can get started with their scientifc worflows with as minimum overhead as possible.

Data

Discover and access

Environmental datasets from different sources, including state offices and university research projects. Access data → Tools

Process and analyse

Use computational tools for data processing, analysis, and environmental modelling. Explore tools → Workflows

Connect and configure

Combine data, tools, and processing steps into configurable and reusable research workflows. Explore the workspace → Reproducibility

Reuse and reproduce

Keep workflows, tools, and data together to support transparent and reproducible scientific analyses. Learn more →

docs.title: From data to results
docs.text:
V-FOR-WaTer connects the different stages of a computational research workflow.

Data → Tools → Workflows → Results

docs.title: A research workflow in four steps
docs.text: 1. Explore  Find datasets and computational tools relevant to your research question.   2. Configure  Select data, tools, parameters, and processing steps to construct your workflow.   3. Run  Execute computational workflows using the selected data and tools.   4. Reproduce  Retain the workflow, tools, and data needed to repeat and build upon your analysis.   One environment. From data to reproducible results.  V-FOR-WaTer connects environmental data, computational tools, and workflows to support transparent and reusable research.

docs.title: tool_whiteboxgis
docs.text: tool_whiteboxgis (Manoj J et al. 2026) is built around the open-source Whitebox Geographic Information System (GIS). WhiteboxTools is a widely used geospatial analysis platform that supports tasks such as watershed delineation, flow accumulation analysis, stream network extraction, terrain characterization, and digital elevation model (DEM) processing (Lindsay, 2016). By packaging these capabilities in a standardized Python container interface, the tool can be integrated into reproducible geoscientific workflows and combined with other containerized processing steps, independently of the execution environment.

docs.title: tool_catflow
docs.text: The tool_catflow container (Manoj J and Dolich, 2025) provides preprocessing tools for the CATFLOW hydrological model (Zehe et al., 2001). It supports the transformation of geospatial raster datasets into hydrological model inputs. These tools build upon an existing CATFLOW preprocessing package developed in R, which has been successfully applied in previous studies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A tool is defined as computational component within the portal that performs a specific geoscientific task. Within the portal we provide access to certain prebuilt tools. The available tools cover a range of geoscientific applications, including geostatistical analyses, geographic information system (GIS) processing, and hydrological model preprocessing.

docs.title: Accessing the Portal and Logging in
docs.text:
The V-FOR-WaTer portal is available at portal.vforwater.de. Logging in is required to access the workspace, use the available tools, and view the history of your tool runs.

To log in:

  1. Click the Login button on the portal homepage.
  2. You will be redirected to the Helmholtz AAI login page.
  3. Choose how you want to sign in:
    • Your institutional account
    • Google
    • GitHub
    • ORCID

If this is your first time logging in, a user registration form will appear after you authenticate. Fill in your details to complete the registration and create your V-FOR-WaTer account. Returning users are taken directly to the portal workspace after logging in.

docs.title: Sections of the Portal
docs.text:
The portal consists of 2 larger sections - Home, and Workspace.

Home is where users land up when accessing the portal. The Home sections gives users the ability to view, visualise, filter, and add data to their Datastore. Understanding the various ways in which users can interact with the data, along with the types of data available in VFORWaTer can be found in Accessing Data.

Workspace allows users to interact with various tools to manipulate their data. A user must be logged in to be able to access the Workspace. Navigating through the workspace can be found in Workspace Navigation. To see how VFORWaTer integrates tools, the current available tools, and how you can use them, check out the general section on Toolbox
